headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel or write-conflict pathway is documented between Plane and Whisper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and broad network content, while Whisper only processes audio files and has no clipboard/MCP/shared-channel surface. No documented bridge shows Whisper outputs being parsed as instructions by Plane, so only an unusual manual copy-paste or file handoff pathway remains.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Whisper transcripts into Plane task fields as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF Plane is configured to treat uploaded text as trusted commands, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Require a human review step before any Whisper transcript is pasted into Plane.
Use a fixed transcript template that separates content from instructions.
Disable free-form task automation on Plane for imported text.
Tag imported audio transcripts as untrusted in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from Whisper outputs into Plane ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, while Whisper only touches audio/speech and has no network egress or filesystem read/write. The pair does not show a shared workspace or third-party upload path, so leakage is limited to manual transfer of sensitive content between the two.
conditions: IF audio transcripts containing sensitive data are manually copied into Plane, that data enters Plane's broader work surface.
IF Plane file uploads include confidential attachments, those contents may be exposed in task artifacts.
mitigations: Restrict Plane projects to non-sensitive data.
Redact transcripts before importing them into Plane.
Use separate accounts/workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Audit uploaded files in Plane before sharing links.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on Plane uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane has no filesystem write capability and Whisper has no filesystem write, shell, git, or network egress capability. With no overlapping mutable resource or write surface, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would change.
IF either profile is extended with shared mutable OAuth scopes, overlapping writes could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts.
Avoid giving either agent shared git or database credentials.
Run them in separate workspaces.
Document any future shared-write integration before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can turn imported content into tasks and roadmaps, but Whisper is only a speech model and does not act on Plane outputs. The pair lacks an automated action-taking chain, so cascading error is mainly a manual workflow risk if Whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative without review.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are imported into Plane without verification, transcription errors can propagate into tasks.
IF Plane automation is configured to create work items directly from transcripts, mistakes can cascade across multiple tasks.
mitigations: Require verification of transcripts before task creation.
Limit auto-generated tasks from speech to draft status.
Add a second reviewer for high-impact items.
Keep source audio linked to each task for auditability.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before Plane accepts transcript-derived tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. Plane and Whisper are both open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU-only, or regulated-data handling that would create a compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into the workflow, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose retention or residency constraints, those must be checked separately.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair by default.
Review deployment residency settings before use.
Document retention rules for transcripts and tasks.
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated data.
